frequency_detail: filed within the first 15 calendar days of the month following the operations; nil filing required, marked SIN MOVIMIENTO
scope: VAT-exempt subjects (sujetos exentos). Until 30 Nov 2025 it also covered responsables inscriptos; RG 5707/2025 removed them, their VAT data now flowing through Portal IVA / IVA Simple (RG 5705/2025) from ARCA's own e-invoice records. Monotributistas, state entities, certain NGOs, newspaper vendors and school cooperatives excluded.
instrument: RG (AFIP) 4597/2019, as amended by RG (ARCA) 5707/2025, art. 2 (scope) and art. 12 (monthly filing)

on_demand_file.note: No named on-request audit-file format (SAF-T equivalent) was identified for Argentina. This is 'not established', not a positive finding of absence.

note_en: Libro de IVA Digital: monthly ledger filed by day 15; from Dec 2025 VAT-exempt subjects only
caveats: The transaction-level duty narrowed sharply on 1 Dec 2025: RG 5707/2025 limits the Libro de IVA Digital to VAT-exempt subjects. What responsables inscriptos now do inside Portal IVA / IVA Simple (F.2051) is a pre-populated VAT determination built from ARCA's e-invoice data, not an independent taxpayer transmission; I could not establish from a primary source whether any residual transaction-level upload duty survives for them. ARCA's own responsables-inscriptos page loaded but is silent on the Libro. Electronic invoicing (CAE authorisation) is the clearance mandate and is excluded here by design.

scope: No taxpayer group is subject to transaction-level or ledger data reporting to the ATO

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or defined audit-file format exists in Australia. General record-retention and production-on-audit rules apply, which is an obligation to keep records, expressly out of scope.

note_en: No transaction reporting to the ATO; Peppol e-invoicing voluntary in B2B; BAS is a summary return
caveats: Best available statement is a vendor/consultancy tracker (VATupdate country booklet), which states plainly that Australia 'does not require businesses to transmit invoice data to the tax authority' and runs a post-audit model; I found no ATO page that asserts the negative, so confidence is medium rather than high. Two adjacent duties were considered and excluded: BAS/GST activity statements are summary returns (out of scope), and Single Touch Payroll is a payroll return (out of scope). One genuine borderline: the Taxable Payments Annual Report (TPAR), a standing annual electronic report of payments made to contractors, lodged by 28 August — ATO page loaded (https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/reports-and-returns/taxable-payments-annual-report). It is payment data transmitted on a schedule, but it is not VAT/transaction ledger data and covers only construction, cleaning, courier, IT, road-freight and security payers. Flagged for the site owner rather than counted.

scope: No taxpayer group is subject to a standing periodic or real-time transaction data transmission duty

on_demand_file.name: SAF-T AT (Standard Audit File-Tax)
on_demand_file.note: BMF's own page frames it as 'Zurverfuegungstellung von Daten auf Datentraegern' — data made available on data carriers when the authority asks. Legal basis is the last sentence of sections 131(3) and 132(3) BAO, inserted by the Abgabenaenderungsgesetz 1998 (BGBl 28/1999), with ministerial guidance from 5 March 1999 onward. There is no filing schedule and no submission channel; it is produced for an audit only.

note_en: No periodic filing; SAF-T AT is produced only on request in an audit, under BAO sections 131(3), 132(3)
caveats: Verified rather than assumed, per the brief: the BMF page confirms the on-request character explicitly. Vendor trackers describing 'SAF-T in Austria' with 'deadlines' are misleading on this point. Not fully established: Austria's cash-register rules (RKSV, section 131b BAO) require a signature-creation device, registration of the register via FinanzOnline and an annual receipt (Jahresbeleg) verified through the BMF Belegcheck app. That is a registration and verification duty, not a stream of transaction data to the authority, so I have not counted it — but I did not reach a primary source on Belegcheck to confirm what data it transmits.
_decision: audit file only: BAO ss.131(3), 132(3): produced for an audit, no filing schedule

frequency_detail: each cash receipt is transmitted to the State Tax Service information system in real time as the sale is recorded
scope: Cash sales to consumers by retail trade, public catering, hotels, medical institutions, barbershops, beauty salons and cosmetic centres; exemptions include newspaper sellers above a turnover share, agricultural market sales and utilities
instrument: Tax Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan arts. 16.1.8 and 220.10; Cabinet of Ministers Decree No. 52 of 14 February 2019 (phased adoption schedule)

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named on-request audit file identified for Azerbaijan; the State Tax Service holds the data centrally through its own portals.

note_en: e-kassa registers send each B2C receipt to the State Tax Service in real time; no periodic ledger file
caveats: The date given is the Cabinet decree that set the phased schedule; the roll-out ran in waves from 2019 (first phase Baku, Ganja, Sumgayit — fuel stations and supermarket chains, per taxes.gov.az post 781, loaded) and I could not establish from a source I read the date on which all remaining taxpayers were captured. e-qaime, the structured electronic tax invoice issued through the State Tax Service portal (mandatory for VAT payers from 1 April 2017, all commercial suppliers from 1 January 2018, new format from 1 January 2020), is the clearance-style e-invoicing mandate and is excluded here by design. Monthly VAT returns by the 20th are summary returns and are excluded. No SAF-T obligation found.
_decision: till-only, excluded: e-kassa transmits each cash receipt to the State Tax Service in real time. Nothing else reports; e-qaime is clearance.

scope: No taxpayer group is subject to transaction-level reporting to the National Bureau for Revenue

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or defined audit-file regime is legislated. Invoices and books must be retained (5 years; 15 years for real-estate records) and are inspected on audit — a record-keeping duty, out of scope.

note_en: No transaction reporting to the NBR; VAT returns only; e-invoicing framework still unpublished
caveats: Sourcing is vendor/consultancy only — VATupdate country booklet and Avalara's Bahrain guide, both loaded, both agreeing that no e-invoicing or e-reporting mandate is in force and that the NBR portal requires manual entry of VAT return figures with no real-time data feed. I reached no NBR page. An e-invoicing framework is anticipated, expected to follow a ZATCA-style phased clearance model, but no law, technical specification, platform or go-live date has been published, so nothing is recorded as 'planned' here. Monthly (supplies above BHD 3m) or quarterly VAT returns are summary declarations and are out of scope.

frequency_detail: near real time after invoice issuance, reported by both supplier and customer; a 5-day window is cited by trackers but the dataset and timing are left to a Royal Decree not yet made
scope: VAT-registered taxpayers on domestic B2B transactions; dual-sided, supplier and customer each report
instrument: Avant-projet de loi modifying the VAT Code, approved by the Council of Ministers on 18 July 2026; sent to the Data Protection Authority and the Council of State for opinion; implementing Royal Decree still to come

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named on-request audit file identified for Belgium. The registered cash register system (GKS/SCE) in hospitality retains data locally for inspection, but I did not reach a source establishing its status as an on-request file, so this is 'not established' rather than a finding of absence.

note_en: Annual client listing of VAT-registered customers via Intervat by 31 March; e-reporting proposed for 2028
caveats: Two things the site owner should see. First, the date: the official Council of Ministers release (loaded) confirms the measure, that both parties report, that it is 'en temps quasi reel', and that it will replace the annual client listing — but it does NOT state 1 January 2028. That date comes from secondary trackers (Comarch and vatcalc, both loaded, both saying 1 January 2028). The instrument is an avant-projet, not enacted law, so date_firm is false. Second, and this is an editorial call: Belgium already has a standing electronic sales listing — the annual client listing of VAT-registered customers, filed via Intervat by 31 March. It is per-customer annual totals rather than transaction-level data, which is why I have not made it the headline status, but it is a scheduled electronic sales listing and the official release confirms the 2028 regime is designed to replace it. The official SPF Finances page for the listing (finance.belgium.be/en/node/1569) would not load — robots.txt blocked on two attempts — so its deadline and legal basis are not confirmed from a primary source here. Structured e-invoicing has been mandatory in domestic B2B since 1 January 2026, but it is decentralised Peppol with no transmission to the authority, so it is not e-reporting.
_decision: The research offered 'planned 2028' on an avant-projet de loi. That fails the enacted test -- but Belgium already has a standing duty the research nearly buried: the ANNUAL CLIENT LISTING of VAT-registered customers, filed via Intervat by 31 March. The Council of Ministers release confirms it exists by saying the 2028 regime will replace it.

frequency_detail: monthly digital fiscal bookkeeping files; EFD ICMS/IPI deadlines are set by each state (the 20th of the following month in Mato Grosso do Sul, and in most states per secondary sources); the EFD-Contribuicoes statutory deadline was not confirmed from a page that loaded
scope: EFD ICMS/IPI: ICMS/IPI taxpayers as designated by each state, phased by size from large industrial establishments (annual revenue from BRL 300m, 1 January 2017) through smaller companies to 2022. EFD-Contribuicoes: private legal entities liable to PIS/Pasep and Cofins
instrument: EFD ICMS/IPI: Convenio ICMS 143/2006 and Ajuste SINIEF 02/2009 (as amended). EFD-Contribuicoes: Instrucao Normativa RFB No. 1.252 of 1 March 2012

on_demand_file.note: Brazil has no SAF-T-style on-request file; the SPED files themselves are the standing submission. Lei 8.218/1991 (as amended by Lei 13.670/2018) requires digital records to be kept and presented to the authority, but that is a record-keeping duty rather than a defined audit file, and I saw it only in a secondary source.

note_en: SPED: EFD ICMS/IPI and EFD-Contribuicoes filed monthly, separate from NF-e clearance
caveats: This is the Poland-style case the brief describes: NF-e/NFS-e clearance is the e-invoicing mandate and is excluded, while the SPED digital bookkeeping files are an additional standing monthly transmission and are what is recorded here. Sourcing was awkward. The federal SPED portal sped.rfb.gov.br is unreachable through WebFetch — it 302-redirects https to http, which is then upgraded back to https, a loop; CONFAZ (confaz.fazenda.gov.br) and the SEFAZ-CE legislation PDF both failed on robots.txt/expired-certificate errors. What did load: the Receita Federal gov.br SPED page for EFD-Contribuicoes (primary, gives IN RFB 1.252/2012 but no deadline), and SEFAZ-MS (https://www.sefaz.ms.gov.br/programas-e-projetos/efd/, a state tax authority, primary) which gives Convenio ICMS 143/2006, Ajuste SINIEF 02/2009, the phase-in from 1 January 2017 for large industrials, and the 20th-of-the-month deadline for that state. The date field (2009-01-01, Ajuste SINIEF 02/2009) is marked not firm because obligation start varies by state and by taxpayer profile and no single national start date was established. Brazil's consumption tax reform (CBS/IBS) is changing the SPED landscape from 2026 — reported that CBS/IBS/IS will not be carried in EFD ICMS/IPI — and I did not establish what replaces or supplements these files.

frequency_detail: monthly file by the 14th of the following month, aligned with the VAT return deadline; a fixed-asset file annually by 30 June of the following year; inventory/stock movements only when the authority asks. The first six monthly files in each phase may be corrected freely until the seventh is filed
scope: Phased by size: 2026 large enterprises with net sales revenue above BGN 300m or taxes and social contributions above BGN 3.5m (measured on 31 December 2023); 2027 large, medium and small enterprises on the same thresholds; 2028 threshold drops to BGN 15m revenue or BGN 1.5m taxes; 2029 all large, medium and small enterprises without threshold; 2030 remaining enterprises, including VAT-registered micro-enterprises
instrument: Tax and Social Security Procedural Code (DOPK), as amended by the State Budget Act for 2025, State Gazette No. 26 of 27 March 2025

on_demand_file.name: SAF-T inventory/stock movements section
on_demand_file.note: Within the same SAF-T regime, the inventory and stock-movement data set is not filed on a schedule — it is supplied only when the revenue authority requests it. This is a genuinely on-request component sitting inside an otherwise periodic obligation, and should not be read as part of the monthly duty.

note_en: SAF-T to the NRA: monthly by the 14th, fixed assets by 30 June; phased by size 2026 to 2030
caveats: No primary source could be read. The NRA's own SAF-T project page and its official SAF-T Q&A PDF (nra.bg) both failed on robots.txt errors. What is recorded rests on two independent consultancy sources that agree closely — PwC Bulgaria (loaded, used as the cited source) and KPMG Bulgaria's March 2025 tax note PDF (loaded), which confirms the vehicle was the 2025 State Budget Act amending DOPK, published in State Gazette 26 of 27 March 2025, first period January 2026 due 14 February 2026, and penalties of BGN 5,000-15,000. Neither identifies the DOPK article numbers, so the instrument field names the act but not the article. Separately and not counted here: Bulgaria's fiscal devices report sales data to the NRA under Ordinance H-18, which would be a second, older e-reporting duty in the POS category — I could not verify it from any source that loaded and have deliberately left it out rather than assert it.

frequency_detail: restaurant sector: transaction data sent 'as soon as the information is known'; remunerated passenger transport: at the end of the trip; adjustments and refunds immediately; if the connection fails, within 48 hours
scope: Quebec only, and only two sectors: restaurants, bars, catering, tourist accommodation and theme parks; and remunerated passenger transport (taxis), which must be on a second-generation certified SRS by 1 January 2026. No federal e-reporting duty and none found in any other province
instrument: Quebec mandatory billing measures administered by Revenu Quebec; the enabling statutory provision was not identified from a source that loaded

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or defined on-request audit file identified at federal level or in Quebec.

note_en: No federal duty. Quebec only: certified SRS sends each sale to WEB-SRM in real time, two sectors
caveats: Read the status with the scope: 'active' is true of Quebec's two mandatory-billing sectors and of nothing else in Canada. Federally there is only the GST/HST return, a summary declaration, out of scope. The Revenu Quebec pages that loaded confirm the data set (transaction modes and types, description of goods or services, amounts and taxes, payment methods, cancellations and corrections), the continuous transmission to WEB-SRM, and the 48-hour fallback. Dates are the weak point: the required-equipment page states it does not give the original start of mandatory billing in restaurants, and the exemption page dealing with establishments installing a certified SRS after 31 May 2025 was rejected by the proxy (HTTP 403), so 31 May 2025 is taken from the corroborating reference on the required-equipment page rather than from the exemption page itself. The predecessor regime, the sales recording module (SRM) introduced in the early 2010s, recorded data locally rather than transmitting it, which is why the WEB-SRM date is used; I could not confirm the SRM's start date from a source that loaded.
_decision: till-only, excluded: WEB-SRM is Quebec only, and only restaurants, bars, catering, tourist accommodation and taxis. No federal duty of any kind.

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T-equivalent audit file identified for Chile. Not verified against SII material - sii.cl could not be fetched.

note_en: DTE/boleta clearance only; RCV ledger is compiled by the SII from DTEs, no separate filing duty found
caveats: PRIMARY SOURCE NOT REACHED. No sii.cl page could be fetched at all: the WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted before work began, and WebFetch refused every sii.cl URL with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (it only accepts URLs on domains already present in the conversation - here fiscal-requirements.com, vatupdate.com, vatit.com and kgd.gov.kz). This is the same tooling wall the first pass hit; it was not overcome. SCOPE REASONING: DTE (factura electronica) and boleta electronica are transmitted to the SII as the document itself, so they are clearance and belong in the e-invoicing box, not here. The question that decides this entry is whether the Registro de Compras y Ventas (RCV) imposes a transmission duty. The best source read (VATupdate, 30 Jun 2026) states the RCV is 'automatically populated using data from issued and received DTEs' and is 'the official digital purchase and sales ledger' - i.e. the SII builds it from documents it already holds, which supports no_mandate. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a taxpayer must supplement the RCV with documents not issued electronically, which would be a residual transmission duty; the SII resolution that replaced the old IECV/libros electronicos (F3327/F3328) with the RCV. CONFLICT BETWEEN SOURCES, unresolved: fiscal-requirements.com states that from 1 August 2022 daily sales summaries are no longer required, while the VATupdate Chile briefing (11 Aug 2025) states electronic receipts must be transmitted within one hour and 'include a Daily Sales Summary'. If a daily summary duty does survive it would be in scope and this entry would be wrong. Both are vendor sources; neither could be checked against the SII. Confidence low per the sourcing standard - vendor trackers only.
_decision: NOT in scope: This is the deciding question and it falls against inclusion. The SII's own FAQ states the register 'es abastecido por los documentos tributarios electrónicos (DTE's) que han sido recibidos por el Ser

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or audit-file obligation identified. The Measures on Accounting Records Administration impose a 30-year retention duty, which is record-keeping and out of scope. Not verified against chinatax.gov.cn.

note_en: Fully digitalised e-fapiao is cleared at issuance; no separate periodic or ledger reporting duty found
caveats: PRIMARY SOURCE NOT REACHED. No chinatax.gov.cn page could be fetched: WebSearch budget exhausted at session start, and WebFetch rejected every non-seed domain with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED. The first pass's limitation therefore stands, though the finding is now corroborated by a SECOND, independently dated VATupdate briefing (10 Dec 2025) as well as the one the first pass used (15 Feb 2026); both state in the same terms that 'there is no separate e-reporting process with later deadlines'. SCOPE REASONING: the fully digitalised e-fapiao is transmitted to the tax authority at issuance and is the invoice - that is clearance, excluded by design, and belongs in the e-invoicing box. Instruments named by the source for the clearance system (not for any reporting duty): STA notice of 24 Nov 2024 for nationwide rollout from 1 Dec 2024; Regulations on the Administration of Invoices as amended by SAT Order No. 37 of 2023; STA Decree No. 33 of 2023. VAT return annexes (fulie ziliao) are part of the periodic VAT return and are excluded by scope. Nothing found on any SAF-T, periodic ledger listing, or cash-register data-transmission mandate. This is a negative finding resting on two vendor briefings plus the absence of any contrary indication; it has NOT been confirmed by silence in the primary material, because the primary material could not be read at all.

frequency_detail: Annual, for the preceding tax year, filed electronically on a DIAN calendar of due dates in the following year
scope: Reporting parties designated in Resolucion 000162 de 2023: withholding agents and VAT collectors, legal entities and individuals above gross-income thresholds expressed in UVT, financial entities, stock exchanges and brokers, foreign permanent establishments, public entities, notaries, chambers of commerce and registry offices
instrument: Estatuto Tributario arts. 623, 623-2, 623-3, 624-633 (incl. 631, 631-2, 631-3); DIAN Resolucion 000162 de 31 October 2023, applicable from tax year 2024

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named standard audit file in Colombia. DIAN may require books, accounts and supporting documents during an audit under the Estatuto Tributario, which is a record-keeping and production duty rather than a defined file. Not separately verified in this pass.

note_en: Annual informacion exogena to DIAN: third-party sales, purchase and VAT listings; no real-time system
caveats: Could not establish a start date for the underlying duty: reporting under art. 631 ET is long-standing and Resolucion 000162/2023 only specifies it from tax year 2024 onward, so `date` is left null rather than guessed. Exact UVT thresholds are NOT reported here: the fetched text of Res. 000162 rendered a 2,400 UVT figure for legal entities and 11,800 UVT for individuals, which does not match the magnitudes practitioners normally cite, and I could not reconcile it against the resolution's own articles - treat any threshold as unverified. Data is reported per third party (per NIT), aggregated rather than per invoice; formats 1001/1005/1006/1007 function as sales/purchase and VAT listings, which is why this is classified in scope. Colombia's DIAN e-invoicing validation and RADIAN event registry are excluded as clearance. Source page loaded normally.

frequency_detail: Monthly from January 2026. Originally due within the first 10 calendar days of the following month; amended so that all 2026 monthly periods may be filed together by 25 January 2027 and, from 2027, within 25 calendar days of the following month
system: D-270 (Informativa Resumen Mensual de Clientes, Proveedores y Gastos Especificos)
scope: Individuals and legal entities, public and private, previously subject to the annual D-151; covers operations with clients, suppliers and specific expenses that are NOT backed by an electronic voucher (comprobante electronico)
instrument: Resolucion MH-DGT-RES-0055-2025 (published 3 November 2025), amended by Resolucion MH-DGT-RES-0010-2026 (published 20 March 2026); partially repeals DGT-R-042-2015 on the D-151

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named standard audit file identified. Accounting records and electronic vouchers must be kept and made available to Tributacion on request under the Codigo de Normas y Procedimientos Tributarios - a record-keeping duty, out of scope here.

note_en: D-270 monthly listing of clients, suppliers and specific expenses not covered by an electronic voucher
caveats: Two Hacienda primary documents were read and both loaded: the CP-14-2026 press release and the Aviso on the Resumen Mensual. They give different deadlines because the second amends the first - the 10-calendar-day rule in MH-DGT-RES-0055-2025 was relaxed by MH-DGT-RES-0010-2026; the amended rule is reported above. The predecessor annual D-151 survives for fiscal year 2025 only, due 25 June 2026. Costa Rica's comprobantes electronicos regime (invoices sent to Hacienda) is excluded as clearance; note the deliberate design of D-270 is to capture only what the clearance system does not see.

frequency_detail: B2C invoices fiscalised in real time at issuance (JIR returned before the invoice is completed); issued e-invoices fiscalised at issuance, self-billed within 5 working days; received e-invoices fiscalised within 5 working days of receipt; rejection data by the 20th of the following month
scope: VAT payers, self-employed persons, profit-tax payers, public administration bodies and local government units operating in Croatia; B2C fiscalisation covers all payment methods, not only cash
instrument: Zakon o fiskalizaciji, Narodne novine 89/25, in force from 1 January 2026

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T in Croatia. Books and records must be produced to the Tax Administration during an audit under the Opci porezni zakon - a record-keeping duty, out of scope here. Not separately verified in this pass.

note_en: Invoice data fiscalised to Porezna uprava as a step separate from the e-invoice; B2C in real time
caveats: Classified as e-reporting, not clearance, on the strength of the Porezna uprava wording: the e-invoice itself travels between the parties via information intermediaries, while fiscalisation is an automated process that EXTRACTS a prescribed data set from the issued or received e-invoice and sends it to the Tax Administration. Two Porezna uprava pages read, both loaded. The European Commission eInvoicing country page for Croatia was also read (loaded) but is stale - it still describes near-real-time reporting as 'expected to begin in 2026' and says there is no real-time reporting system, which is no longer accurate; it was therefore not used as the cited source. Croatia has had cash-transaction fiscalisation since 2013 under the earlier Zakon o fiskalizaciji u prometu gotovinom; the 2013 start date was not verified against a primary source in this pass, so only the 2026 instrument is dated above.
_decision: Fiskalizacija 2.0 fiscalises issued and received E-INVOICES, not just B2C tills -- that limb is invoice-data reporting.

frequency_detail: No scheduled or real-time transmission of transaction or ledger data. VAT returns and VIES recapitulative statements only, both of which are excluded as periodic declarations.
scope: n/a - no reporting population

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T and no named standard audit file. Books and records must be kept and produced to the Commissioner of Taxation on request, which is a record-keeping duty and expressly out of scope. Not verified against a Cyprus Tax Department primary page.

note_en: No transaction reporting, SAF-T or real-time system; periodic VAT return and VIES only
caveats: This is a negative finding and no Cyprus Tax Department page states the absence, so it rests on the European Commission country page, which loaded and says explicitly 'Currently, there is no real-time reporting system in Cyprus' and 'VAT Real-time reporting system mandate: NO'. That is an EU institution page, not the Cypriot authority or gazette, hence source_kind secondary and confidence medium. Searches restricted to tax.gov.cy and mof.gov.cy surfaced no SAF-T or e-reporting announcement. The 2026 Cyprus tax reform package was checked at search level only and appears not to introduce transaction reporting; that was not confirmed against the enacted legislation.

frequency_detail: Legal entities and VAT groups monthly, by the 25th day after the end of each calendar month regardless of their VAT period; natural persons by the same deadline as their VAT return, so monthly or quarterly
scope: All persons registered for VAT in the Czech Republic holding a CZ VAT ID that carry out reportable transactions; filing is mandatory in electronic form
instrument: Act No. 235/2004 Coll. on Value Added Tax, sections 101c-101k

on_demand_file.note: The Czech Republic has no SAF-T and no named standard audit file. VAT records kept under section 100 of the VAT Act must be produced during a tax inspection, which is a record-keeping duty and out of scope.

note_en: kontrolni hlaseni: invoice-level VAT listing, monthly by the 25th; quarterly for some individuals
caveats: Financni sprava page loaded normally and confirms invoice-level detail (issued and received tax documents including simplified invoices), the 1 January 2016 start and the sections 101c-101k basis. The control statement is distinct from the VAT return and is therefore counted; the VAT return itself is excluded. The former EET electronic records of sales (cash-register reporting) is understood to have been terminated with effect from 1 January 2023, which would remove a second Czech reporting duty, but that was NOT verified against a primary source in this pass - treat it as unconfirmed.

frequency_detail: No standing duty to transmit transaction or ledger data on a schedule. Accounting material reaches authorities through statutory filings and through requests during audit or control.
scope: n/a - no reporting population

on_demand_file.name: SAF-T (Danish standard) / regnskabsmateriale under bogforingsloven
on_demand_file.note: This is an on-request obligation, not a periodic filing. Under bogforingsloven a business must record transactions in a digital bookkeeping system and must make its accounting material available to public authorities on request during audit or control. Separately, providers of digital bookkeeping systems must be able to generate, import and export a SAF-T standard file and make it available to the user; registered systems must support SAF-T version 2.0 by 1 January 2027, with version 1.0 (header file) otherwise. The digital bookkeeping requirement extends on 1 January 2026 to non-accounting-obligated businesses with net turnover above DKK 300,000 in two consecutive financial years and to financial-sector companies.

note_en: No periodic transmission; digital bookkeeping with SAF-T export produced for authorities on request
caveats: The brief's suspicion is confirmed: Denmark's obligation is of the on-request/capability kind and is recorded only in on_demand_file. Two Erhvervsstyrelsen pages were read and both loaded. The SAF-T page states plainly that the requirement is on system PROVIDERS to be able to generate, import and export the file - a capability requirement - and neither page describes any periodic submission. Neither page names the receiving authority for an on-request delivery (Erhvervsstyrelsen vs Skattestyrelsen), so that is left unstated rather than guessed. An attempted fetch of https://erhvervsstyrelsen.dk/digital-bookkeeping failed (URL not reachable/not in provenance) and is not relied on.
_decision: audit file only: bogfoeringsloven: the duty is on the SYSTEM to be able to export it

frequency_detail: Within the first 15 days of the month following the month invoiced, submitted through the DGII Oficina Virtual
scope: All taxpayers, including those under special regimes (Norma General 07-2018 art. 2). e-CF issuers under Ley 32-23 still file 606 for the traditional series-B NCF they receive, but are relieved of 607 and 608 because e-CF data reaches DGII electronically; 607 also becomes due again for contingency periods when e-CF cannot be issued
instrument: Norma General 07-2018 (DGII), arts. 2-8

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named standard audit file identified. DGII may require books and supporting documents during an audit under the Codigo Tributario - a record-keeping duty, out of scope. Not separately verified in this pass.

note_en: Formats 606/607/608/609: monthly purchase, sales and cancelled-voucher listings to DGII by the 15th
caveats: Start date left null deliberately: the 606/607 reporting duty predates Norma General 07-2018, which consolidates and restates it, and I could not establish the original commencement date from a primary source. Content per NG 07-2018: 606 costs and expenses plus ITBIS/ISR withholdings; 607 sales and operations; 608 cancelled fiscal vouchers with reasons; 609 payments abroad for services. Three DGII sources read, all loaded (the Norma PDF, the Formatos de Envio de Datos page, and the DGII help-community answer on e-CF issuers). The DGII page states the 606 deadline as 'before the ITBIS declaration deadline'; the Norma's own art. 8 rule of the first 15 days is reported above as the authoritative one. The e-CF clearance regime under Ley 32-23 is excluded as e-invoicing.

caveats: PRIMARY SOURCE NOT REACHED. No nta.go.jp page could be fetched: WebSearch budget exhausted at session start; WebFetch rejected nta.go.jp with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED. The finding is however now supported by TWO independent secondary sources rather than the first pass's one: (a) fiscal-requirements.com, a fiscalisation specialist, which classifies Japan as a 'non-fiscal' jurisdiction with 'no mandatory obligation to transmit transaction data to the tax authority' in real time or periodically, no mandated POS fiscalisation and no device certification; and (b) the VATupdate Japan booklet (17 Jul 2026), which states Japan has 'no SAF-T, no periodic transaction-level e-reporting, and no real-time reporting' and that Japanese Consumption Tax is filed from the taxpayer's own records. Two sources of different type agreeing on a negative is the strongest position obtainable without the NTA. SCOPE REASONING: the Qualified Invoice System (from 1 Oct 2023) governs invoice content, issuer registration and retention - there is no transmission of invoice data to the NTA - so it is out of scope for this box and, being non-transmitting, is a matter for the e-invoicing box only. The consumption tax return is a summary declaration and is excluded by scope. Confidence marked low per the sourcing standard because no National Tax Agency page was read, although this is the best-corroborated of the five negatives.

It is not a reporting step distinct from issuing the invoice. For context only, the instruments the source attaches to that clearance mandate are Income Tax Law No. 38 of 2018 art. 23, Regulation No. 34 of 2019 on organising and controlling invoicing affairs, and the amended Billing and Control Regulation No. 2 of 2025, with the system voluntary from Dec 2022 and mandatory for all B2B, B2C and B2G from 1 April 2025; those dates belong to the e-invoicing box, not to this one. note_en: Online cash registers transmit fiscal data via an OFD; start date, interval and scope not established
caveats: WHAT IS NOW PRIMARY-SOURCED, and this is an advance on the first pass: the State Revenue Committee (KGD) itself publishes, on the page cited, the register of fiscal data operators (ofd_reestr.docx), the protocol for transmitting data from cash registers to the OFD server (v2.0.4) and the 2026 state register of cash register models - so the existence of an operating online-KKM/OFD data-transmission regime rests on the tax authority's own material, not on a vendor. A second KGD page, https://kgd.gov.kz/ru/content/prikazy-2018-goda-1 (loaded), names the three Ministry of Finance orders of February 2018 listed in the instrument field, including No. 206 which sets the list of activities for which a KKM with data fixation and transmission function is required - which corroborates that the duty was phased in by activity type. WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, and why the fields are null: the date the transmission duty commenced, the statutory transmission interval, and which taxpayer categories are currently in scope. The operative texts are all published by KGD as .docx attachments (prikaz_pravil_po_kkm_-rus.docx, the OFD protocol, the ТИС order) and WebFetch returned '[binary data]' for every one of them; adilet.zan.kz and other gazette routes are on domains WebFetch refuses (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED) and the WebSearch budget was exhausted at session start, so no alternative route to the text existed. SCOPE REASONING: (1) ЭСФ / IS ESF electronic invoices are clearance - the invoice is transmitted to the state platform as the invoice - and are excluded, belonging in the e-invoicing box. (2) СНТ (сопроводительные накладные на товары) is a goods-movement document issued into the same platform, i.e. document issuance for transport, not periodic transaction or ledger reporting; excluded here and better placed in an e-transport box. (3) VAT Forms 300.07 and 300.08, the registers of sales and purchase invoices, are annexes to the periodic VAT return Form 300.00 and, per the VATupdate Kazakhstan briefing of 28 Oct 2025 (secondary), taxpayers whose invoices are all electronic are no longer required to complete them; treated as part of the VAT return and therefore out of scope, but flagged because a sales/purchase listing filed on a schedule would otherwise be in scope and the site owner may wish to take a different view. (4) The online cash-register duty is in scope as cash-register transaction reporting to the authority. Status is given as 'active' because the existence of the duty is established from primary material; frequency, date and scope are left null rather than guessed. Confidence low overall because the quantitative particulars remain unsourced.

note_en: eSales: monthly CRM/POS sales to the BIR by the 8th/10th; quarterly SLSP listings; EIS/ESRS from 2027.
caveats: ADDS a duty the previous pass missed. Alongside eSales there are the quarterly Summary Lists of Sales and Purchases, filed electronically through RELIEF - a sales/purchase listing filed on a schedule, which the brief lists as in scope. Corroborated indirectly: VATupdate's Philippines briefing notes that taxpayers on the EIS 'are exempted from filing the traditional Summary List of Sales (SLS)', which presupposes the duty exists for everyone else. frequency is therefore 'varies' rather than 'monthly'. eSales is CONFIRMED as in scope, being POS transaction reporting transmitted to the authority on a schedule, but note it is machine-level monthly gross sales plus receipt ranges, not transaction-level data - materially narrower than myDATA or SII, and the country sheet should not imply otherwise. DATE LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: no source read states when either duty commenced, and it has not been inferred; the previous pass's guess at RR 5-2005 is not repeated, and the source here attributes eSales to RR 10-99 and RMO 29-2002 instead, which is itself an unresolved conflict. FORTHCOMING AND DISTINCT: under RR 11-2025 as amended by RR 26-2025, covered taxpayers must issue structured e-invoices and transmit the data to the BIR's Electronic Invoicing/Receipting System 'within 3 calendar days from the date of transaction', with the compliance deadline extended to 31 Dec 2026 and enforcement from 1 Jan 2027; scope is large taxpayers, e-commerce sellers, exporters, POS/CAS users and registered business enterprises. That regime is transmission of the invoice as the invoice, so on the brief's rules it belongs in the e-invoicing box, not here - but it will displace eSales and SLS for those taxpayers, so the two boxes need to be reconciled before 2027. CONFIDENCE LOW: no bir.gov.ph page could be fetched. No primary source was reachable for any of the five; that is a tooling limit, not a finding about the law, and these records should be re-run once search or an unrestricted fetch is available.

Decreto-Lei 198/2012 is cited by the AT as the instrument but no source I read gave its commencement date, and a vendor guide (InvoiceXpress) instead pointed at Portaria 321-A/2007 and 2008, which conflates the file format with the reporting duty. `date` is therefore left null rather than guessed. Confidence reduced to medium for that reason only; the deadline, scope and instrument are from a primary AT page that loaded. The annual accounting SAF-T is recorded under on_demand_file because as of now it is produced on request / for IES pre-fill rather than filed on a schedule — if the postponement lapses this becomes a second standing periodic duty.

on_demand_file.note: No audit-file obligation established. Qatar has no VAT in force, so there is no VAT ledger or audit file to produce.

note_en: No VAT and no transaction reporting duty; e-invoicing law approved by Cabinet May 2026, not yet gazetted
caveats: No standing duty to transmit transaction or ledger data to the General Tax Authority exists today: as of 27 July 2026 Qatar has no VAT law in force, no VAT registration and no VAT returns. The Council of Ministers approved a draft e-invoicing law and its executive regulations on 6 May 2026; PwC Middle East (https://www.pwc.com/m1/en/services/tax/middle-east-tax-news-alerts/2026/qatar-e-invoicing-law-and-regulations-approved.html, secondary, loaded) confirms the approval but states that detailed provisions are unreleased, no implementation dates are set and NO distinct e-reporting obligation is mentioned. A vendor briefing (VATupdate, secondary, loaded) claims B2C invoices will have to be reported within one or two days and that go-live is expected around 1 January 2027, but describes these as expert projections with no official date; I therefore do not record a planned e-reporting duty. I could not reach any gta.gov.qa page — no official Qatari source was read. Revisit once the law is published in the Official Gazette.

frequency_detail: monthly or quarterly following the taxpayer's VAT period (quarterly for taxpayers not registered for VAT), due on the last calendar day of the month following the reporting period; the assets section is annual
scope: phased by taxpayer category: large taxpayers from 1 January 2022 (or 1 July 2022 if newly classified), medium from 1 January 2023, small from 1 January 2025; sole traders, self-employed persons, family enterprises and public institutions are excluded
instrument: OPANAF nr. 1783/2021, under art. 59^1 of Law 207/2015 (Fiscal Procedure Code)

on_demand_file.name: D406 stocks section (secțiunea de stocuri)
on_demand_file.note: The stocks section of the SAF-T schema is the only part filed solely at ANAF's express request, and ANAF has begun requesting it from selected taxpayers. Verified on https://www.avocatnet.ro/articol_68021/ (legal news site, secondary, loaded); the deadline once requested was not stated in that source. All other D406 sections are filed on the periodic schedule.

note_en: D406 SAF-T filed monthly or quarterly by the last day of the following period; small taxpayers since 2025
caveats: RO e-Factura clearance is deliberately excluded as the e-invoicing mandate. Grace periods apply to first filings (up to six months for monthly filers, three for quarterly). I did not verify from a primary source the separate start date reported for non-established VAT-registered taxpayers (1 January 2025) and have folded it into the small-taxpayer wave rather than assert it. RO e-Transport (reporting of high-risk goods movements) is a separate transport-declaration duty and is not counted here as transaction or ledger data reporting.

frequency_detail: simplified (B2C) tax invoices must be reported to the FATOORA platform within 24 hours of generation; standard tax invoices are cleared before issue and are not counted here
system: FATOORA (Phase 2 Integration Phase — reporting model for simplified invoices)
scope: phased in waves by VAT-taxable revenue; wave 25 covers taxpayers whose VAT-taxable revenue exceeded SAR 187,500 in 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025, who must integrate by 1 February 2027
instrument: E-Invoicing Regulation and the Controls, Requirements, Technical Specifications and Procedural Rules issued by the ZATCA Board of Directors on 4 December 2020

on_demand_file.note: No named periodic or on-request audit file (no SAF-T equivalent) established. ZATCA may request records under its general audit powers, but no defined file format is prescribed.

note_en: Simplified B2C invoices reported to ZATCA within 24 hours; standard invoices are cleared, not reported
caveats: EDITORIAL FLAG: this entry is a judgement call and the site owner should check it. Saudi Phase 2 has two flows. Standard (B2B/B2G) invoices are CLEARED — ZATCA stamps them before they reach the buyer — which the brief puts out of scope. Simplified (B2C) invoices are issued to the customer first and then transmitted to ZATCA within 24 hours, which is a transmission step distinct from issuing the invoice and so reads as e-reporting; but it sits inside the same e-invoicing mandate rather than covering transactions outside it, so it could equally be recorded in the e-invoicing box. I have reported it here with that caveat rather than silently including or excluding it. Confidence is medium for that classification reason; the underlying facts are from a ZATCA primary guideline that loaded, and the wave 25 criteria from https://zatca.gov.sa/en/MediaCenter/News/Pages/Wave25-E-invoicing.aspx (primary, loaded). The 1 January 2023 date is the start of wave 1; each taxpayer's own obligation begins on its wave date, notified at least six months in advance.
_decision: Simplified tax invoices are issued to the customer and then transmitted to FATOORA within 24 hours. They are invoices in ZATCA's own vocabulary, not till summaries; standard invoices are cleared and stay in the mandate box.

frequency_detail: two duties: electronic recording of VAT calculation in the SEF is done after the end of each tax period, by the 12th day of the following calendar month; separately, fiscal receipt data are transmitted to the Tax Administration in real time at the moment of retail sale (within five days if the connection is down)
system: Elektronsko evidentiranje obračuna PDV (SEF); e-fiskalizacija (Sistem za upravljanje fiskalizacijom)
scope: VAT recording in the SEF: VAT debtors under the VAT Law, public-sector entities and voluntary SEF users. E-fiscalisation: every taxpayer carrying out retail trade, defined broadly as any supply to individuals regardless of payment method, including vending machines
instrument: Zakon o elektronskom fakturisanju, čl. 4 and 4a ("Sl. glasnik RS" 44/2021, as amended through 109/2025); Zakon o fiskalizaciji, čl. 8 ("Sl. glasnik RS" 153/2020, 96/2021, 138/2022)

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named audit-file obligation established for Serbia.

note_en: SEF electronic VAT records due by the 12th of the following month; POS receipts sent to the SUF in real time
caveats: SEF invoice exchange itself (Sistem e-Faktura) is deliberately excluded as the e-invoicing mandate; what is recorded here is the SEPARATE duty to record the VAT calculation electronically in the SEF, plus e-fiscalisation. The `date` given is the start of the VAT-recording duty for private-sector VAT debtors; the public sector started 1 May 2022 (Article 24). E-fiscalisation has its own dates: the Law on Fiscalisation applies from 1 November 2021 with a transition period to 30 April 2022, verified on https://www.paragraf.rs/propisi/zakon-o-fiskalizaciji-republike-srbije.html (secondary, loaded). Both sources are the Paragraf Lex legal database reproducing the consolidated statutory text with Official Gazette citations, not the gazette itself — I could not load an efaktura.gov.rs or pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs page. Confidence is high because the statutory articles were read directly, but source_kind is honestly marked secondary. The VAT-recording rules were substantially rewritten with effect from 1 January 2025 (individual and collective records); I did not separately verify that amendment's detail.
_decision: Electronic recording of the VAT calculation in the SEF is a ledger duty. E-fiskalizacija is the till limb.

frequency_detail: Peppol-transmitted invoices reach IRAS on a real-time or near-real-time basis as the invoice is sent to the customer; solution-extracted data may be scheduled but must reach IRAS by the earlier of the GST return filing date or the filing due date
scope: phased: newly incorporated companies applying for voluntary GST registration from 1 November 2025; all new voluntary GST registrants from 1 April 2026; new compulsory registrants and existing businesses with annual supplies up to S$200,000 from 1 April 2028; up to S$1m from 1 April 2029; up to S$4m from 1 April 2030; above S$4m from 1 April 2031
instrument: IRAS GST InvoiceNow Requirement, administered under the GST Act and its regulations

on_demand_file.name: IRAS Audit File (IAF)
on_demand_file.note: A listing of sales and purchases supporting the figures in the GST return, generated from the taxpayer's accounting software and provided to IRAS during an audit. It is not filed periodically. The IRAS page on GST audits that I loaded did not mention the IAF at all; the description is taken from Microsoft Learn's Dynamics 365 documentation quoting IRAS (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/localizations/singapore/apac-sgp-iras-audit-file, secondary, loaded), which itself hedges on whether submission is audit-only. Treat the on-request characterisation as probable, not verified against IRAS.

note_en: GST InvoiceNow: invoice data sent to IRAS via Peppol; phased from Nov 2025, all GST registrants by 2031
caveats: Both sales and purchase invoice data are transmitted. A voluntary soft launch ran from 1 May 2025; I did not verify that date from the loaded FAQ. The IRAS web page for the requirement returned only navigation, not content — the phased dates and mechanics come from the IRAS FAQ PDF (version 16 Oct 2025, primary, loaded). I could NOT establish the specific statutory instrument imposing the requirement; the instrument field describes the administering framework only and should not be printed as a legal citation. Confidence is medium on that basis and because of the IAF sourcing above; the phase dates themselves are high confidence.

frequency_detail: kontrolný výkaz filed within 25 days after the end of each VAT period — monthly or quarterly according to the taxpayer's VAT period, or on the same day as the return if filed earlier; separately, eKasa online cash registers send receipt data to the Financial Administration in real time (stored locally and sent within 48 hours if the 2-second response window is exceeded)
scope: kontrolný výkaz: persons registered for VAT under §4, §4a, §4b, §5 and §6 of Act 222/2004 (those registered under §7 or §7a are exempt, as are payers filing a nil return or reporting only exempt supplies). eKasa: entrepreneurs required to record retail takings
instrument: §78a of Act No. 222/2004 Coll. on VAT (kontrolný výkaz, first period January / Q1 2014); Act No. 289/2008 Coll. as amended December 2018 (eKasa)

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T and no named audit file established for Slovakia. Accounting records must be made available under general audit powers, but no prescribed file format was found.

note_en: Kontrolný výkaz: transaction-level VAT listing filed with each return; eKasa sends POS receipts in real time
caveats: The kontrolný výkaz is counted as e-reporting because it is a transaction-level sales/purchase listing filed electronically in XML on a schedule, not a summary declaration — it is filed alongside, and separately from, the VAT return. eKasa dates verified on the Financial Administration's own text of the December 2018 amendment (primary, loaded): existing electronic cash register users had to migrate by 1 July 2019, new registrants from 1 April 2019. FORTHCOMING AND UNRESOLVED: a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and real-time e-reporting regime (IS EFA, five-corner Peppol model) is intended from 1 January 2027, extending to cross-border in 2030, with the kontrolný výkaz and EC Sales Lists to be abolished (reported variously as June 2030 or on introduction). I could NOT establish whether the enabling VAT Act amendment has been enacted: Accace (loaded) says it awaits parliamentary approval, Global Indirect Tax Management (loaded) describes a July 2025 draft in consultation, Comarch (loaded) reports Financial Administration guidelines of May 2026 without stating legislative status, and VATupdate (loaded) reports a 5-day reporting window for received invoices without citing the act. All four are secondary. Do not print a 2027 e-reporting date as firm on this evidence.
_decision: Kontrolny vykaz is a transaction-level VAT listing filed with each return. eKasa is the till limb.

frequency_detail: invoice data are sent to FURS over the internet and confirmed with a unique invoice identifier (EOR) at the moment the cash invoice is issued
scope: persons who keep business records, issue invoices for goods or services and receive payment in cash (gotovinsko poslovanje), with statutory exemptions
instrument: Zakon o davčnem potrjevanju računov (ZDavPR), Uradni list RS št. 57/2015 of 31 July 2015

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T and no named audit file established for Slovenia. General duties to keep documentation and to supply data to the tax authority on request exist under ZDavP-2 (art. 32 and 39), but no prescribed file format was found, so this is not recorded as a defined on-request audit file.

note_en: Cash invoices confirmed with FURS in real time; no SAF-T and no periodic ledger filing
caveats: The only standing transmission duty found is fiscal verification of cash invoices, which the brief's scope note expressly admits as POS transaction reporting. Slovenia has NO SAF-T, no periodic transaction listing and no VAT ledger filing. A transition period ran from 2 January 2016 to 31 December 2017 during which a bound pre-numbered invoice book was an alternative; electronic devices with an EOR became compulsory for everyone from 1 January 2018 — so 2016-01-02 is the start of the regime, not the point of universal electronic transmission. IMPORTANT FOR THE E-REPORTING BOX: the draft B2B e-invoicing law originally carried a separate obligation to report invoices to FURS within 8 days of issuance; that reporting requirement was REMOVED from the revised draft, and the mandate was pushed to 1 January 2027 (Comarch, secondary, loaded, dated 28 March 2025 and reflecting a draft as at 11 February 2025). I could not confirm from any source read whether that law has since been adopted or whether the reporting element stayed out, so no planned e-reporting duty is recorded. Confidence is medium for that reason. The primary FURS source loaded; pisrs.si returned a JavaScript shell and the FURS .doc FAQ returned binary, so neither could be read.
_decision: till-only, excluded: Davcno potrjevanje racunov fiscalises cash invoices in real time. Slovenia has no SAF-T and no ledger filing at all.

frequency_detail: the e-Tax Invoice is issued to the buyer first and its details are transmitted to the National Tax Service by the day following issuance (automatic where Hometax is used)
scope: all corporations since January 2011; sole proprietors phased in by falling revenue thresholds — KRW 1bn from 2012, KRW 300m from July 2014, KRW 200m from July 2022, KRW 100m from July 2023 and KRW 80m from July 2024
instrument: Value-Added Tax Act (부가가치세법) art. 32 and its Enforcement Decree

on_demand_file.note: No SAF-T or named audit file established for Korea. Sales and purchase aggregate tax-invoice lists (합계표) are submitted with VAT returns, but those are summary schedules attached to the return rather than an on-request audit file.

note_en: e-Tax invoices transmitted to the NTS by the day after issuance; no separate periodic audit file
caveats: Counted as e-reporting because Korea is not a clearance regime: the invoice is issued to the buyer and only then transmitted to the NTS, a step distinct from issuing it. The site owner may still prefer to record it in the e-invoicing box, since the same act does both — flagging rather than deciding. The cited source is a Korea National Tax Service presentation (October 2020) hosted on the BRITACOM site; it loaded and is marked primary on authorship, but it is dated and does not cite the VAT Act article. The NTS English page https://www.nts.go.kr/english/na/ntt/selectNttInfo.do?nttSn=77577 would NOT load (robots.txt fetch timed out), so no current official page was read. The current KRW 80m threshold, the January 2011 corporate start, the VAT Act art. 32 basis and the fallback of a monthly summary by the 10th of the following month come from a vendor tracker (VATupdate country booklet, 28 July 2026, secondary, loaded). Confidence medium on that basis; the mechanism itself is high confidence.
_decision: The e-Tax Invoice is issued to the buyer first and its details go to the NTS by the following day. Not clearance, and not a till feed.

frequency_detail: invoice records supplied within 4 days of issue, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and national holidays
scope: taxpayers on a monthly VAT settlement period: turnover above EUR 6m, VAT groups, REDEME (monthly refund register) registrants, and fuel deposit holders from 1 Jan 2025; voluntary for others
instrument: Real Decreto 596/2016 of 2 Dec 2016 amending art. 62.6 and the record-book articles of the VAT Regulation (RD 1624/1992); technical specifications in Orden HFP/417/2017

on_demand_file.name: Registros de facturacion of a non-VERI*FACTU SIF
on_demand_file.note: Under the RD 1007/2023 billing-software rules, a taxpayer whose system is NOT in VERI*FACTU mode keeps the billing records locally and sends them to the AEAT only when the administration requires them, through a simplified automated procedure (AEAT wording: 'en caso de que se requieran por parte de la Administracion Tributaria dichos registros, los mismos podran ser directamente enviados'). Confirmed on the AEAT VERI*FACTU general-questions page, which loaded.

note_en: SII: invoice records supplied to AEAT within 4 working days; large taxpayers, VAT groups, REDEME.
caveats: Start date and instrument taken from the BOE text of RD 596/2016 (loaded); the AEAT general-information page (loaded) gives the scope and the 4-day rule but not the start date or article references. VERI*FACTU is deliberately NOT counted as a standing reporting duty: continuous transmission of billing records to the AEAT is one of two permitted modes, the other being local retention with on-request sending, and SII taxpayers are excluded from the regime altogether. VERI*FACTU/SIF adaptation deadlines were pushed to 1 Jan 2027 (corporate income tax filers) and 1 Jul 2027 (all others) by Real Decreto-ley 15/2025 of 2 Dec 2025 (AEAT notice, loaded). The regional TicketBAI regimes in the Basque provinces and Navarra, which do transmit, were not verified in this pass and are not reflected above.

scope: not applicable - no standing transaction or ledger reporting duty

on_demand_file.note: No standardised audit file. Sweden has never adopted SAF-T; the SIE format is a market accounting-exchange standard, not a filing or production obligation. Records must be made available in an audit under general procedural rules, but no named file was identified.

note_en: No transaction reporting duty; Skatteverket cites EU cross-border digital reporting from 2030.
caveats: Skatteverket's own page states there is currently no obligation ('transaktionsbaserad rapportering' is not mandatory), that intra-EU cross-border B2B transactions are to be reported digitally from 2030 under the EU ViDA rules, and that a government inquiry appointed 5 Feb 2026 is examining domestic e-invoicing. That 2030 duty is EU-level and applies to cross-border transactions only, so it is not recorded as a Swedish planned mandate here - flagging it for the site owner's editorial call. Separately, a 2026 change letting Skatteverket inspect accounting systems remotely during audits was reported by vatcalc.com (secondary, loaded); it is audit access, not a filing duty, and the article's own dates are internally inconsistent (parliamentary approval 6 May 2026, stated effect 1 April 2026), so it is not relied on.

frequency_detail: within 2 days where the buyer is not a business, within 7 days where the buyer is a business; unused invoice number ranges and settings within 10 days of the start of the next period
system: eGUI upload to the MOF E-Invoice Integration Service Platform (dianzi fapiao cunzheng)
scope: business entities that issue electronic uniform invoices (eGUI)
instrument: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act art. 32-1 as amended, in force 1 Jan 2025; penalty art. 48-2 (NT$1,500-15,000 per breach)

on_demand_file.note: No named on-request audit file identified. This is 'not established' rather than a positive finding of absence - the Regulations Governing the Use of Uniform Invoices could not be read (see caveats).

note_en: eGUI data uploaded to the MOF platform within 2 days (non-business buyer) or 7 days; VAT Act art. 32-1.
caveats: Classification call: Taiwan's eGUI is not full clearance - the invoice is issued to the buyer and the data is separately transmitted to the MOF platform for cunzheng (archiving/certification) within 2 or 7 days - so it is recorded here as reporting rather than as the invoicing mandate. An upload duty existed before 2025 under the Electronic Invoice Implementation Guidelines (widely cited as 48 hours / 7 days); art. 32-1 raised it to statute with penalties from 1 Jan 2025, and the 1 Jan-30 Jun 2025 grace period for allowance documents is on the same source. Sources that would not load: law.moj.gov.tw Regulations Governing the Use of Uniform Invoices (robots.txt disallowed), einvoice.nat.gov.tw guidance (403), law-out.mof.gov.tw Implementation Guidelines (loaded but did not reproduce the time limits), ntbna.gov.tw e-invoice section (loaded, no time limits). Whether the bi-monthly business tax return carries transaction-level media files of issued and received GUIs was not established.
_decision: eGUI data is uploaded to the MOF platform within 2 or 7 days after the invoice reaches the buyer -- a separate step.

frequency_detail: e-Arsiv invoice data reported to GIB by 23:59 the following day; separately, e-Defter berat files uploaded monthly, by the end of the third month following the month concerned
scope: e-Arsiv: taxpayers required to be in e-Fatura had to join e-Arsiv by 1 Jan 2020; for other taxpayers invoices above TRY 3,000 in 2025, and all invoices without a threshold from 1 Jan 2026 (1 Jan 2027 for simplified-basis taxpayers). e-Defter: e-Fatura users, companies subject to independent audit, taxpayers on the balance-sheet basis, and taxpayers notified individually by the administration
instrument: VUK Genel Tebligi No. 509 (e-Arsiv application, defined as covering electronic preservation, presentation and 'raporlama', section V.8 Raporlama); Elektronik Defter Genel Tebligi (Sira No: 1) as amended

on_demand_file.name: e-Defter ledger files (XBRL GL)
on_demand_file.note: Only the berat - an approval/hash summary - is uploaded to GIB on the monthly cycle. The ledger files themselves stay with the taxpayer in XBRL GL format and are produced to the authorities on request. Source: edefter.pro (secondary, loaded), explicit: 'the whole ledger does not go to GIB, only this approval summary does'.

note_en: e-Arsiv invoice data reported to GIB by 23:59 next day; monthly e-Defter berat; e-Fatura excluded.
caveats: e-Fatura is clearance and is excluded. The important nuance for the site owner: e-Defter transmits a berat certificate on a schedule, NOT the ledger data - if the site's test is transmission of data, e-Defter arguably belongs in on_demand_file rather than in the standing duty, and it is recorded in both fields above so the choice stays open. The 23:59-next-day e-Arsiv deadline is from fiscal-requirements.com (vendor tracker, loaded), not from a primary text: VUK 509 loaded and confirms e-Arsiv covers 'raporlama' with a section V.8 Raporlama and the 1 Jan 2020 start, but the excerpt returned did not include the deadline itself. The e-Defter berat deadline (end of the third month following) is from workon.com.tr (secondary, loaded); the GIB infographic PDF (primary, loaded) confirms scope and that berats are uploaded monthly but gives no calendar deadline. An elective three-month / provisional-tax-period berat option is believed to exist but could not be confirmed from any source that loaded, so it is not asserted. Sources that would not load: edefter.gov.tr communiqué PDFs (robots.txt disallowed), resmigazete.gov.tr (robots.txt fetch failed, TLS certificate verification error), gib.gov.tr HTML pages (returned headers only). Form Ba / Form Bs monthly purchase and sales listings above TRY 5,000 were abolished from 1 Oct 2024 (vatcalc.com, secondary, loaded) and are therefore not counted.

frequency_detail: the reporting timeline is left to a further decision of the Minister and has not been set; the separate duty to transmit the invoice to the recipient is within 14 days of the business transaction
system: UAE eInvoicing System - reporting to the FTA via an Accredited Service Provider
scope: Phase 1 from 1 Jan 2027: persons with annual revenue of AED 50m or more. Phase 2 from 1 Jul 2027: persons below AED 50m. Phase 3 from 1 Oct 2027: government entities. Voluntary participation from 1 Jul 2026. B2C excluded until the Minister decides otherwise
instrument: Ministerial Decision No. 243 of 2025 art. 6(6) (duty to report electronic invoices and credit notes to the Authority); Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025 (implementation phases)

on_demand_file.note: No named on-request audit file identified in the eInvoicing decisions; general record-keeping duties under the Tax Procedures Law were not examined in this pass.

note_en: MD 243/2025 art. 6(6): invoices must be reported to the FTA; phase 1 go-live 1 Jan 2027.
caveats: Art. 6(6) of MD 243/2025 makes reporting to the Authority a duty distinct from art. 6(5) transmission to the recipient, which is what puts the UAE in scope here rather than being purely an invoicing mandate - but the decision expressly defers the reporting timeline to the Minister, so frequency is genuinely unknown and is left null rather than guessed at 'near real time'. Phase dates are from MD 244/2025 (primary, loaded). A MoF news item (loaded) confirms the phase 1 ASP appointment deadline moved from 31 Jul 2026 to 30 Oct 2026 while the 1 Jan 2027 go-live is unchanged.

scope: not applicable - no standing transaction or ledger reporting duty

on_demand_file.note: No standardised audit file exists in the UK (no SAF-T equivalent). HMRC obtains records under its general information powers; that is a production power, not a named file obligation, and it was not separately verified in this pass.

note_en: No reporting duty; e-invoicing mandated from 2029, real-time reporting explicitly deferred.
caveats: The consultation response states the UK will introduce mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT invoices from 2029 and, on reporting, that the government 'will consider the case for introducing some form of RTR (Real-Time Reporting). However, this will not be implemented in 2029 but would be implemented once e-invoicing use was well established.' Making Tax Digital for VAT is deliberately not counted: it transmits the nine-box VAT return, a summary declaration, and its digital record-keeping requirement is a keeping duty. MTD for Income Tax quarterly updates were not examined; they are categorised income and expense totals rather than transaction-level data, but the site owner may want that checked.

scope: not applicable - no standing transaction or ledger reporting duty found at federal or state level

on_demand_file.name: Machine-sensible records under Rev. Proc. 98-25
on_demand_file.note: Machine-sensible accounting records must be retained and 'made available to the Service upon request and must be capable of being processed'. Applies to taxpayers with assets of USD 10m or more at year end, to smaller taxpayers where the information is not available in hardcopy or requires computer recomputation, and where the District Director gives notice. Production only - there is no scheduled filing of the file.

note_en: No transaction-level reporting duty; federal and state filings are summary returns.
caveats: There is no VAT and no federal transaction-level reporting regime; state sales and use tax returns are summary declarations and are excluded by the brief. Two things could not be closed out before the session's web search budget was exhausted, which is why confidence is medium and not high: (a) the current status of the state-level 'notice and report' duties imposed on non-collecting out-of-state sellers, several of which required customer purchase detail to be reported to the state and most of which were repealed or fell away after Wayfair; (b) whether any individual state now requires transaction-level schedules with its return. Third-party information returns such as Form 1099-K are filed by payors about other people's transactions, not by a business about its own ledger, and fall outside the definition used here.
_decision: audit file only: machine-sensible records produced to the IRS on request

frequency_detail: one consolidated report per calendar day, sent within the first 18 hours of the following business day, and required even for days with no transactions
scope: every electronic issuer (emisor electronico) of CFE. VAT taxpayers are required to hold electronic issuer status from 1 Jan 2025, with exceptions including lower-income agricultural producers, construction-only operators, non-resident income tax payers, fully exempt taxpayers and Monotributo taxpayers
instrument: Resolucion DGI N. 798/012, numeral 20 (Obligacion de informar)

on_demand_file.note: No named on-request audit file identified. Not established either way in this pass.

note_en: CFE issuers send DGI a consolidated daily report within 18 hours of the next business day.
caveats: The CFE itself is authorised and received by DGI and is treated as the e-invoicing mandate, not counted here; the reporte diario under numeral 20 is a separate consolidated transmission listing CFE and contingency documents issued, by type, date, branch and numbering consumed, including voided numbers. The date given is the date of Resolucion 798/012 (8 May 2012, published 15 May 2012); the resolution has been amended many times - the foreign-currency conversion rule dates from 1 Nov 2022 and some provisions took effect as recently as 2025 - and the exact commencement of numeral 20 in its present wording was not pinned down. A separate monthly obligation exists for e-Resguardos (numeral 23: at least one document per month per withholding subject), which is a withholding document duty rather than transaction reporting and is not counted.

frequency_detail: by the 20th of the month following the reporting month
scope: retail trade and services, phased: 1 Jan 2020 for sellers of alcohol, tobacco, medicines, fuel and natural gas; 1 Aug 2020 for annual turnover above 5bn soum; 1 Jan 2021 above 100m soum; 1 Jan 2022 all remaining, with exemptions for remote and hard-to-reach settlements determined annually
instrument: VAT return form approved by joint order of the Ministry of Finance and the State Tax Committee, registered with the Ministry of Justice as No. 3126 of 21 January 2019; new form version code 10006_45 applies from 1 January 2026; auto-preparation introduced by Law No. ZRU-1108 of 25 December 2025

on_demand_file.note: No named on-request audit file identified. Not established either way in this pass.

note_en: Online and virtual cash registers transmit each retail sale to the tax authority; phased 2020-22.
caveats: The electronic invoice system (ESF, elektron hisob-faktura, factura.soliq.uz) registers invoices in the state information system before they are final and is therefore clearance, excluded by the brief; the cash-register regime is what puts Uzbekistan in scope. Confidence is medium because the phasing and the receipt-content rules come from the lex.uz decree text (primary, loaded) but the wording confirming real-time transmission of each sale to the tax authority was summarised rather than quoted, and the Tax Committee's own page (soliq.uz/page/onlayn-nkm) could not be fetched (robots.txt fetch timed out). A vendor booklet (vatupdate.com, secondary, loaded) states Uzbekistan has no SAF-T and no separate periodic transaction file, and that VAT returns are pre-filled by the authority from e-invoice data from 1 Jan 2026 under Law ZRU-1108 of 25 Dec 2025 - pre-filling by the authority is not a taxpayer reporting duty and is not counted. Whether the monthly VAT return still carries invoice registers as annexes was not established.
_decision: recovered by the content-not-envelope rule: an invoice-level annexe to a VAT return is a listing, not a summary return

caveats: Coded e-invoices are authenticated by the tax authority and are the clearance mandate, excluded by the brief; art. 22 is the additional duty for the uncoded regime and is what is recorded here. Source grading: art. 22 was read in an unofficial English translation on vanbanphapluat.co (loaded), not on an official Vietnamese government site, so source_kind is secondary. Decree 70/2025/ND-CP, dated 20 Mar 2025 and reported in force from 1 Jun 2025, re-issues art. 22 under a revised heading; its full current wording was not read, so the sectoral split and deadlines above reflect the Decree 123 text as translated and may have been amended. The 1 Jul 2022 nationwide start date is from fiscal-requirements.com (vendor tracker, loaded), not from the decree text returned, which gave only the 19 Oct 2020 signing date. Cash-register e-invoices connected to the tax authority (from 1 Jun 2025) were not established in enough detail to state whether they add a distinct data-transfer duty.
_decision: Form 01/TH-HDDT transfers uncoded e-invoice data to the GDT. Coded invoices are clearance and stay in the mandate box.
